item.title: Intraocular Pressure Change After Cataract Surgery in Normal-Tension Glaucoma and Nonglaucomatous Eyes: Predictors of Postoperative Response
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Cataract surgery significantly reduced IOP in nonglaucomatous eyes. Although the mean 6-month reduction was not significant in medically treated NTG eyes, responses varied substantially. In the overall cohort, preoperative characteristics may help identify eyes more likely to benefit.

item.title: Steering nanometric reductive-oxidative Fenton-like cycle for PFAS mineralization
item.description: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs), known as "forever chemicals," have highly stable C─F bonds that render them resistant to destruction by conventional water treatment processes. Here, we developed a destructive technology that does not require external photo-, electro-, or heat energy input, relying simply on Fenton-like cycles (peroxymonosulfate activation) under nanometric spatial confinement. Unlike the ordinary activation process, confinement shielded peroxymonosulfate radicals...

item.title: Spheroid-laden hydrogels with dual biomimetic intra- and perispheroidal niches for enhanced bone healing
item.description: Stem cell spheroid-hydrogel platforms offer promise for bone defect repair, but implantation-associated oxidative stress, poor vascular ingrowth, and insufficient osteogenic cues limit their clinical translation. Here, we developed dual-NICHE (dual niche-instructive construct for bone healing and engraftment), a gelatin methacryloyl hydrogel containing human adipose-derived stem cell spheroids with spatially distinct intra-/perispheroidal niches. Within a single construct, these two niches...

item.title: Non-invasive, high-precision, and independently controllable neuromodulation via optimized multiple temporal interference stimulation
item.description: Non-invasive neuromodulation is an important approach in clinical and translational neuroscience, yet existing techniques remain limited in precisely and flexibly targeting spatially distributed brain regions. Temporal interference stimulation (TIS) enabled non-invasive selective targeting; however, conventional implementations lack sufficient spatial focality, steerability, and scalability for network-level modulation. Here, we introduce optimized multiple temporal interference stimulation...

item.description: ObjectivesThis study investigated the association between hospital quality of care and the adoption of mobile-based personal health record (m-PHR) applications.MethodsA nationwide cross-sectional study included Korean hospitals with more than 100 beds. Data on m-PHR adoption were collected in 2022, and hospital quality data were obtained from the 2021 national hospital quality evaluation reports from the Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service (HIRA). item.title: Effects of sparse array geometry and element arrangement on low-intensity transcranial focused ultrasound
item.description: Sparse arrays are used in low-intensity transcranial focused ultrasound, but the effects of element arrangement, aperture and coverage are not well defined. We simulated nine spherical-cap arrays at 250 kHz, combining 50, 60 and 70 mm aperture radii with 40, 50 and 60% coverage (active-element fraction of the cap area), using 8 mm elements, a 100 mm radius of curvature and a fixed nominal drive of 15 W. A scalar hybrid angular spectrum model with straight-ray phase correction was applied to...

item.title: Real-time instance segmentation of spine endoscopy images using a YOLO-V11 deep convolutional neural network
item.description: CONCLUSION: This research contributes to AI-driven surgical guidance systems, with potential applications in robotic-assisted spine surgery. The developed model enables real-time navigation, improving intraoperative decision-making and enhancing surgical outcomes. In particular, our YOLO-V11-based framework extends prior single-structure or lower-frame-rate multi-element approaches by delivering real-time multi-class instance segmentation of instruments, anatomical structures, and bleeding sites...

item.description: This scoping review maps the recent applications of generative adversarial network (GAN)-based methods in medical imaging from 2021 to 2025. The aim was to provide an evidence map of recent original studies, focusing on methodological categories, imaging modalities, anatomical targets, application domains, translational-readiness evidence, and trustworthiness gaps. The scoping review was conducted and reported in accordance with the PRISMA extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). PubMed,...

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The favorable occlusion rates and acceptable complication profiles suggest that TTDCs are safe and effective for treating small IAs.

item.title: Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation and Mortality in Pediatric Medical Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation
item.description: Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) using extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is increasingly used in pediatric refractory cardiac arrest. This study investigated the association between ECPR and mortality in pediatric patients receiving venoarterial ECMO (VA-ECMO) for medical indications. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients aged 28 days to <18 years who received VA-ECMO at a tertiary referral children's hospital between January 2010 and May 2025. The...

item.title: Comparative outcomes of multi-port versus single-port laparoscopic surgery in adhesive small bowel obstruction
item.description: CONCLUSION: Transumbilical single-port laparoscopic surgery for adhesive small bowel obstruction is safe and effective in appropriately selected patients. When evaluated under ITT principles and adjusted for disease severity, single-port access provides equivalent 30-day safety while significantly accelerating functional gastrointestinal recovery and reducing hospital stay compared with conventional multiport laparoscopy.

item.title: Does Loneliness Condition the Association Between Restless Sleep and Later Depressed Mood? A Three-Wave Study of Korean Adults Aged 57 and Older
item.description: Sleep problems and loneliness are established risk factors for later-life depressive symptoms, but whether loneliness conditions their prospective association is rarely examined. Using three biennial waves of the Korean Longitudinal Study of Ageing (2020-2024; N = 5,266; aged 57-98), we tested whether loneliness (2022) moderated the association between restless sleep (2020) and depressed mood (2024), each a single CES-D10 item, net of baseline depressed mood. Restless sleep (b = 0.063) and...

item.title: Temporal Trends in Antiplatelet Strategies After PCI: A Nationwide Study by Presentation and Bleeding Risk
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Antiplatelet strategies evolved, although real-world practice only partially reflected changing guideline recommendations. Major bleeding declined over time, whereas major adverse cardiac event trends were less uniform.

item.title: A comparison of treatment effects between modified miniscrew-assisted rapid palatal expanders with distalizers and pendulum appliances
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The MMD group showed greater bodily distalization and less rotation of the maxillary first molars and less labial tipping of the incisors than the PA group. MMD can be considered as a treatment option for maxillary expansion and molar distalization.

item.title: Iron-Chelating Nanoparticles Enable Cytoprotection against Ferroptosis In Vitro and In Vivo
item.description: Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death driven by lipid peroxidation and mitochondrial dysfunction, contributes to degenerative and ischemic diseases, yet strategies that simultaneously control labile iron and oxidative stress remain limited. Here, we developed mesoporous polydopamine nanoparticles (PDNs) with intrinsic antioxidant and iron-chelating properties. PDNs scavenged free radicals, reduced intracellular Fe2+ levels, preserved mitochondrial function, and rescued...

item.title: Direct Optical Lithography of Intrinsically Stretchable Colloidal Emissive Nanocrystals
item.description: Realizing high-resolution stretchable displays requires emissive materials that combine photopatternability with intrinsic stretchability. In colloidal nanocrystal films, however, the network formation needed for precise patterning often restricts molecular mobility, creating a fundamental trade-off with mechanical compliance. Here, we address this challenge using a benzophenone-based dual-crosslinker strategy that forms an elastomeric nanocrystal network. The tetrafunctional small-molecule...

item.title: Bifunctional Ligand Engineering of Aminophosphine-Derived InP Quantum Dots for Efficient Green Electroluminescence
item.description: Tris(dimethylamino)phosphine ((DMA)(3)P)-derived InP QDs commonly suffer from surface oxidation, undercoordinated surface atoms, and inefficient interfacial charge injection, which limit their optical and electroluminescent performance. Herein, we report a bifunctional ligand-engineering strategy using phenethylamine (PEA) to simultaneously regulate the surface chemistry and interfacial electronic properties of green-emitting InP QDs. The amine group of PEA coordinates to undercoordinated...

item.title: Guidelines for Diagnosis, Reporting and Management of Intraductal Papillary Neoplasm of the Bile Duct (IPNB): Recommendations of Bangkok Consensus Meeting
item.description: CONCLUSION: These recommendations should aid in cross-national standardized classification, diagnosis, reporting, and management of IPNBs, and serve as a launching pad for further studies.

item.description: PurposeThe purpose of this study was to identify and validate NANDA-International (NANDA-I) diagnoses, Nursing Interventions Classification (NIC), and Nursing Outcomes Classification (NOC) relevant to caring for people living with HIV over the age of 50.MethodsWe conducted a content validation survey among 28 human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)/acquired immunodeficiency syndrome nursing experts. item.title: Literature-Derived Network and Semantic Mapping of Pain Catastrophizing and Traditional East Asian Medicine Pattern Constructs
item.description: CONCLUSION: The analysis identified a pattern-dominant, literature-conditioned structure rather than strongly pair-specific mappings. Results were sensitive to graph-strength normalization. They characterize conceptual proximity in published texts and graph structure; they do not establish diagnostic equivalence, clinical validity, causality, treatment efficacy, or treatment guidance.

item.title: Health Decision-Making Among Women Survivors of Intimate Partner Violence: A Scoping Review
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Health decision-making among IPV survivors was shaped by intersecting individual, structural, and healthcare-system factors that varied across contexts, suggesting the need for integrated, context-sensitive responses beyond individual-level approaches.

item.title: Oncologic outcomes according to the extent of prostatic involvement after radical cystectomy: A comparison of prostatic urethral and stromal invasion
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: PSI was associated with significantly worse oncologic outcomes than PUI following radical cystectomy. These findings suggest that recurrence and metastatic progression are driven primarily by the extent of prostatic invasion rather than diversion type. ONB after a negative DFS appears oncologically acceptable in carefully selected patients, although PSI warrants closer surveillance.

item.title: Noninvasive Treatment of Infraorbital Fat Protrusion With Patch-Mediated Laser-Induced Shock Wave Therapy: A Case Series
item.description: CONCLUSION: In this case series, a single session of LISWT delivered through a diamond particle acoustic patch was associated with short-term improvement in photographically graded infraorbital contour and was well tolerated over 2 months.

item.title: Real-world comparative effectiveness and persistence of ustekinumab versus vedolizumab across cohort mean age in Crohn's disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis with meta-regression
item.description: CONCLUSION: In CD, UST was favored over VDZ for both effectiveness and persistence, and its effectiveness advantage appeared to attenuate with increasing cohort mean age. Because these are study-level data, this age-related pattern warrants confirmation through patient-level analyses and dedicated studies in older adults, in whom direct comparative evidence remains limited.

item.description: This study investigated the molecular mechanisms by which carbon-ion beam irradiation (IR), either alone or in combination with paclitaxel (PTX) or nab-PTX, induces cell death in pancreatic cancer (PC) cells in vitro. Human PC cell lines, PANC-1 and MiaPaCa-2, were treated with carbon-ion beam IR alone or combined with PTX/nab-PTX. Cell viability, caspase-3/7 activity, and the expression of apoptosis-, autophagy-, and angiogenesis-related genes and proteins were analyzed using quantitative...

item.title: First record of the beetle family Limnichidae Erichson, 1846, based on Pelochares ryukyuensis M. Satô, 1966 (Coleoptera, Byrrhoidea) from Korea
item.description: BACKGROUND: Limnichidae Erichson, 1846 is a small family within the superfamily Byrrhoidea, comprising approximately 400 species. Although it is a widely distributed taxon, it had not been formally recorded from Korea prior to this study. The newly-recorded species, Pelochares ryukyuensis M. Satô, 1966, was known only from Japan (Honshu, Shikoku, Kyushu, Tsushima, Koshikijima Islands, Ryukyu Islands) and China (Taiwan).

item.title: Clinician-informed design requirements for CKD-specific digital therapeutics: A focus group study with nephrologists to guide clinically integrated intervention development
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This study identified clinician-informed design requirements for CKD-specific digital therapeutics through focus group interviews with nephrologists. The findings indicate that nephrologists prioritize safety-related functions, disease-specific content, and workflow-integrated design as key requirements that current disease-agnostic digital health tools do not adequately address. Future studies should incorporate patient perspectives and prospective prototype evaluation to validate...

item.description: Staphylococcus aureus infections pose a serious public health threat due to increasing antibiotic resistance, pointing to the need for an effective vaccine. Here, we introduce an eco-evolutionary game framework in which the payoffs to cooperators and defectors are directly shaped by the fraction of free space, the unoccupied environmental capacity that determines opportunities for growth, colonization, and resource renewal. In our model, free space evolves in...

item.title: Efficacy and Safety of High-Intensity Focused Ultrasound for Aesthetic Contouring and Skin Tightening: A Systematic Review
item.description: CONCLUSION: HIFU may provide a noninvasive option for body contouring, skin tightening, and cervicofacial rejuvenation, with generally favorable changes across objective and patient-reported outcomes. More standardized comparative studies are needed to better define the magnitude and durability of treatment-related changes.

item.title: Skin Brightening and Anti-Aging Effects of Human Umbilical Cord Wharton's Jelly-Derived Mesenchymal Stem Cell Conditioned Media and Herbal Extract: A Randomized, Controlled Double-Blinded Trial
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The cosmetic formulation containing human umbilical cord Wharton's jelly-derived mesenchymal stem cell-conditioned media and herbal extract significantly improved pigmentation, texture, and pore appearance compared to the vehicle control over the eight-week treatment period, supporting its potential for the short-term management of early photoaging and pigmentation-related concerns.

However, the noncomparative design, nonstandardized photography, nonblinded GAIS assessment, follow-up attrition, and absence of pure-PDO or pure-PP comparator groups prevent attribution of early or late effects to either material and preclude claims of superiority or synergy. In patients with advanced skin excess or cervicofacial ptosis, surgical...

item.title: Mechanotransduction of Collagen Biostimulators: Comparative Signaling and Implications for GLP-1 RA-Associated Facial Aging
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Mechanotransduction-active collagen biostimulators provide a biologically plausible rationale for addressing facial volume loss, although current clinical evidence remains limited and no studies have directly enrolled GLP-1 RA-associated facial aging patients. A conceptual severity-stratified framework warrants prospective validation.

item.title: Nervonic Acid Promotes Skin Regeneration by Enhancing Collagen Synthesis and Suppressing Inflammation
item.description: CONCLUSION: NA promotes regenerative responses in dermal fibroblasts by enhancing cell migration and collagen production, while suppressing pro-inflammatory cytokine production. It has potential as an active cosmetic ingredient for supporting skin regeneration.

item.title: New Elastic Fiber Formation Can Be Induced by Intradermal Injection of Transparent Porcine-Derived Type I Atelocollagen in Mice
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Transparent porcine-derived Type I atelocollagen enhanced skin thickness, promoted elastic fiber regeneration, and restored youthful dermal architecture while demonstrating favorable biocompatibility through transient M2 macrophage-mediated tissue remodeling. These findings support the potential of transparent porcine-derived atelocollagen as an effective skin booster for skin rejuvenation, warranting further investigation of its molecular mechanisms and long-term clinical efficacy.

item.title: Multi-Parametric Biophysical Analysis for Evaluating Suitability of Energy-Based Devices and Injectables
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Multi-parametric biophysical stratification successfully translates complex interactions into actionable clinical guidelines. Recognizing negative synergy zones highlights the absolute clinical necessity of spatiotemporal sequential tracking rather than indiscriminate concurrent combinations, paving the way for data-driven precision aesthetics.

item.title: Beyond Volumization: Repositioning Hyaluronic Acid Fillers as Anatomy-Guided Structural Support Tools in the Era of Biostimulators
item.description: CONCLUSION: HA fillers should not be viewed as obsolete because of overfilling. Appropriate patient selection, anatomy-guided planning, conservative dosing, region-specific product selection, and vascular safety may allow HA to function as a structural support tool. The future of HA filler treatment is not less HA, but better-directed HA.

item.title: Facial Lifting and Skin Rejuvenation Using a Dual-Wavelength Picosecond Nd:YAG Laser in Asian Skin: A Prospective Pilot Study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Dual-wavelength picosecond Nd:YAG laser treatment progressively improved skin elasticity, skin tone, and overall skin quality with a favorable safety profile, supporting its potential for nonablative facial lifting and skin rejuvenation.

item.title: A Prospective, Active-Controlled Split-Face Clinical Trial Evaluating the Incremental Aesthetic Benefits of a Glutathione-Containing Booster in a GHK-Conjugated Spicule Regimen
item.description: CONCLUSION: The GHK-conjugated spicule base regimen improved multiple facial aging indicators, and the booster-inclusive intensive regimen produced statistically greater short-term improvements in this small split-face trial. Because the booster was multi-ingredient and the release mechanism was not directly measured in vivo, these findings should be interpreted as regimen-level clinical evidence rather than proof of glutathione-specific redox cleavage.

item.title: A Sterile Folliculocentric Acneiform Eruption Mimicking Infection After Hair Transplantation: Clinical Pattern Recognition and a Proposed FUE Epidermal Cap-Angle Mechanism
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This sterile folliculocentric eruption appears to represent a technique-associated inflammatory reaction that may mimic infection in the early postoperative period. To our knowledge, this is the first characterization of this discrete, early-onset sterile entity as distinct from previously described post-transplant folliculitis, supporting a non-antibiotic, stewardship-oriented management approach. The proposed epidermal cap-angle mechanism is presented as a testable hypothesis.

item.title: Recombinant Human Collagen in Clinical Medicine
item.description: CONCLUSION: Recombinant human collagen is a platform biomaterial rather than a single product class. Its clinical value depends on matching collagen type, molecular format, formulation, degradation profile, mechanical behavior, and biological indication. In aesthetic medicine, its strongest future role may be regenerative matrix restoration rather than simple volume replacement. IncobotulinumtoxinA is free of complexing proteins and has a low antigenic protein burden, which may favor its use for intradermal injection. However, direct long-term comparative evidence for aesthetic intradermal treatments is lacking.

item.description: CONCLUSION: In this 36-patient cohort, a single-session hybrid CaHA-PN skin booster protocol was associated with significant improvements in facial skin quality and cheek wrinkle severity at 6 months, with high patient-reported improvement and a favorable safety profile. Prospective controlled studies are needed to define comparative efficacy and to optimize dosing schedules.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The suction-type biomimetic patch significantly enhanced multiple skin parameters compared with ampule application alone. These findings support the potential of structure-mediated, noninvasive suction interfaces as delivery-enhancing platforms in cosmetic dermatology.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This preclinical study demonstrates that CPM-HA20G achieves rapid tissue hydration via a dual hydration mechanism and is well tolerable with favorable tissue integration. Glycerol was found to play a unique role in enhancing hydration without inducing stress responses, providing antioxidative capacity and cell protection. These findings provide a mechanistic basis for the clinical efficacy of CPM-HA20G.

item.title: Nonsurgical Aesthetic Improvement of the Neck: A Multimodal, Experience-Based Algorithmic Approach
item.description: CONCLUSION: Nonsurgical neck rejuvenation is best approached as a staged, multimodal, lower-face-inclusive process rather than treatment of an isolated cervical concern. The proposed framework is intended as a practical decision-support tool for individualized treatment planning, not as a validated or prescriptive treatment protocol.

item.title: Impact of a National Antimicrobial Stewardship Pilot Program on Hospital Antimicrobial Stewardship Implementation: A Two-Year Nationwide Survey in Korea
item.description: CONCLUSION: Pilot program participation was the factor most strongly associated with perceived ASP implementation. Differences by respondent profession and hospital type may reflect role-specific visibility of ASP activities as much as institutional capacity, and warrant cautious interpretation. These findings support continued expansion of the national ASP pilot program.

item.description: CONCLUSION: The optimized IFN-γ ELISPOT assay established in this study provides a sensitive, reproducible, and safe method for monitoring VZV-specific CMI. This standardized protocol is well-suited for evaluating vaccine efficacy and assessing disease susceptibility in immunocompromised children in clinical settings.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Combining cilostazol with standardized Ginkgo biloba extract may offer a multi-target approach for stroke survivors with SVD or PSCI. Its clinical use should acknowledge the limitations of indirect evidence; prospective randomized trials are needed to establish long-term efficacy and safety.

item.title: EUS-Guided Drainage of Postoperative Fluid Collections: A Multicenter Comparison of Plastic Stents, SEMS, and LAMS
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: EUS-guided drainage for POFC demonstrated high clinical success with a low adverse event rate. No statistically significant difference in clinical outcomes was detected across stent types. However, this comparative finding should be regarded as exploratory and requires confirmation in larger prospective studies. Until robust evidence becomes available, stent selection may reasonably be individualized according to the procedural preference and clinical scenario.

item.title: Evaluation of a multifunctional phantom for geometric, image quality, and dosimetric constancy of megavoltage electronic portal imaging devices
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: MZ Slab supported geometric, image-quality, radiation-field, qualitative MLC, and portal-dosimetry assessments within a single-phantom QA workflow. Measurements on three linacs characterized within-session reproducibility and week-to-week consistency over four weeks. Longer observation and deliberate perturbation testing are required to establish action limits and fault-detection sensitivity.

item.title: Microbial exopolysaccharides as mediators of gut microbiota-host interactions
item.description: In recent years, the gut microbiota has emerged as an important regulator of metabolic health and a potential therapeutic target for metabolic disorders, including obesity and diabetes. Among the diverse metabolites and bioactive compounds produced by gut bacteria, bacterial exopolysaccharides (EPS) have attracted increasing attention. This is largely due to their structural similarity to dietary fiber and their potential prebiotic effects on the intestinal environment. Accumulating evidence...

item.title: Comparison of Ocular Surface Abnormalities and Tear Film Dysfunction Among Patients with Sick Building Syndrome, Allergic Conjunctival Disease, and Healthy Controls
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Patients with SBS exhibited greater tear film dysfunction and ocular surface abnormalities than patients with allergic conjunctival disease despite similar tear IgE levels. Symptom severity was more strongly associated with tear film dysfunction and ocular surface abnormalities than with tear IgE, suggesting that tear film disruption is a key mechanism underlying the ocular manifestations of SBS.

item.title: TLR5 drives metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis through lipid- and flagellin-induced hepatocyte injury signaling
item.description: Liver fibrosis is a strong predictor of clinical outcomes in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). Fibrosis is a consequence of persistent liver cell injury and inflammation in which Toll-like receptors (TLRs) play a key initiating role. Here, we test the hypothesis that TLR5 is involved in the development of MASH and fibrosis using a combination of clinical data from multiple independent patient cohorts, single-cell liver transcriptomics, and human in vitro and ex vivo...

item.title: IncD is an essential type III effector that supports Chlamydia propagation
item.description: The obligate intracellular bacterium Chlamydia trachomatis is the most common bacterial cause of sexually transmitted infections worldwide. C. trachomatis replicates within a specialized intracellular compartment, the inclusion, whose membrane contains bacterial inclusion membrane (Inc) proteins, a family of type III secreted effectors that manipulate host pathways to support bacterial development and nutrient acquisition. Acquisition of host sphingolipids is essential for C. trachomatis...

item.title: National statement of clinical and therapeutic approach of patients with systemic sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease in Belgium on behalf of the Flemish network on rare connective tissue diseases
item.description: CONCLUSION: Despite the availability of international guidelines for SSc-ILD, differences in therapeutic access, reimbursement policies and the organization of multidisciplinary care necessitate country-specific guidance. This Belgian expert statement aims to support harmonized, equitable and timely access to optimal care for patients with SSc-ILD.

item.title: An antiaromatic expanded porphyrin-based supramolecular polymer
item.description: Herein we report the self-assembly of an antiaromatic expanded porphyrin into a supramolecular polymer. This assembly proceeds cooperatively through hydrogen bonding to afford columnar arrays displaying photoconductivity.

item.title: Gene Burden Testing for Rare and Genetic Disease Studies: A Practical Beginner-Oriented Workflow
item.description: Gene burden testing is a practical analytic framework for evaluating whether multiple rare variants within a gene, transcript, or biologically defined variant set are collectively associated with disease. This strategy is especially useful in rare disease and sequencing-based genetic studies because most individual rare variants are too uncommon to achieve adequate statistical power on their own, whereas aggregating them into a biologically meaningful set can increase the ability to detect...

item.title: Cytosolic and Mitochondrial Ca<sup>2+</sup> Imaging in Drosophila Dopaminergic Neurons
item.description: The ATP-producing organelle, mitochondrion, controls cellular or synaptic Ca^(2+) concentrations through temporal uptake of Ca^(2+) outside of the mitochondria. Although intracellular Ca^(2+) influx occurs during neuronal activity, a persistently higher concentration of intracellular Ca^(2+) is neurotoxic. Healthy mitochondria ensure rapid Ca^(2+) uptake, which is necessary for proper neuronal activity. Mitochondrial Ca^(2+) buffering activity decreases in aged or sick neurons. In this chapter,...

item.title: Electroretinogram Recording Using Drosophila Parkinson's Disease Models
item.description: The neuronal activity evoked by light stimulation is a useful indicator to evaluate early neural dysfunction. ElectroRetinoGraphy (ERG) is a relatively simple electrophysiological technique to measure these responses and is widely used in clinical settings, primarily for visual and optic nerve disorders, and has also been applied to the assessment of neurodegenerative diseases such as Parkinson's disease. In addition, ERG represents a highly useful and convenient research tool for studying...

item.title: Analysis of Dopaminergic Functions in Drosophila
item.description: Dopaminergic (DA) neurons regulate various physiological functions, including motor function, emotion, learning, sleep, and arousal. Degeneration of DA neurons in the substantia nigra of the midbrain causes motor disturbance in Parkinson's disease (PD). Studies on familial PD have revealed that a subset of PD genes encode proteins that regulate mitochondrial function and synaptic dynamics. Drosophila is a powerful model of PD, whereby genetic interactions of PD genes with well-conserved cellular...

item.title: The Functional Assessment of LRRK2 in Caenorhabditis elegans Mechanosensory Neurons
item.description: The nematode Caenorhabditis elegans (C. elegans) is a powerful model organism to systematically analyze the functions of genes of interest in vivo. Especially, C. elegans nervous system is suitable for morphological and functional analyses of neuronal genes due to its optical transparency of the body and well-established anatomy, including neural connections. The C. elegans ortholog of Parkinson's disease-associated gene LRRK2, named lrk-1, has been shown to play a role in the regulation of...

item.title: Assessment of Cytotoxicity of α-Synuclein in Budding Yeast Using a Spot Growth Assay and Fluorescent Microscopy
item.description: The budding yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae is a model organism amenable to both genetic analysis and cell biology. Due to these advantages, yeast has provided platforms to examine the properties of pathogenic proteins involved in human diseases. The methods used to examine the cytotoxicity and intracellular localization of α-Synuclein, a human neuronal protein implicated in Parkinson's disease, using yeast have been described herein. These methods are readily accessible to researchers or...

item.title: Drug Delivery to the Brain of Parkinson's Disease Mouse Using an Osmotic Pump and Methods for Evaluating Motor Performance
item.description: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a common neurodegenerative disorder that is characterized by progressive resting tremors, rigidity, bradykinesia, gait disturbances, postural instability, and dementia. The symptoms of PD are closely linked to the degeneration of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta. The loss of these neurons in some mouse models of PD results in abnormal motor performance, including abnormal limb-clasping reflexes, abnormal footprint patterns, and lower rotarod...

item.title: Deep Brain Stimulation Using Animal Models of Parkinson's Disease
item.description: The use of deep brain stimulation (DBS) as a therapy for neurological disorders, especially Parkinson's disease (PD), is widely applied in the field of functional neurosurgery. Both the subthalamic nucleus and the globus pallidus interna are major targets for PD. Experimental DBS is performed using animal models to evaluate new indications and promote advancements in technology. In this article, we reviewed our experience with the concept of experimental DBS, including its development and...

item.title: Application of a Tissue Clearing Method for the Analysis of Dopaminergic Axonal Projections
item.description: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by the progressive loss of dopaminergic (DA) neurons within the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc). Quantitative analysis of neuronal loss, including neuronal processes, axons, and dendrites, would advance the understanding of the pathophysiology of PD. ScaleS, an aqueous tissue clearing method, provides stable tissue preservation while maintaining potent clearing capability, allowing quantitative three-dimensional (3D)...

item.title: Common Marmoset Model of Alpha-Synuclein Propagation
item.description: Understanding the propagation of alpha-synuclein (αS) aggregates is critical for elucidating the pathological mechanisms of synucleinopathies such as Parkinson's disease, dementia with Lewy bodies, and multiple system atrophy. Here, we describe a protocol for generating a nonhuman primate model of αS propagation by intracerebral injection of synthetic αS preformed fibrils (PFFs) into the common marmose (Callithrix jacchus). This protocol allows phosphorylated αS pathology and its propagation to...

item.title: α-Synuclein Propagation Mouse Models of Parkinson's Disease
item.description: Parkinson's disease (PD) is pathologically characterized by intraneuronal α-Synuclein (α-Syn) inclusions called Lewy bodies (LBs) and by the loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNpc). Autopsy studies have suggested that Lewy pathology initially occurs in the olfactory bulb and enteric nervous system and subsequently spreads throughout the brain in a stereotypical manner. Recent studies have demonstrated that templated fibrillization and intercellular dissemination...

item.title: Midbrain Slice Culture as an Ex Vivo Analysis Platform for Parkinson's Disease
item.description: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative disorder of the motor system. It is characterized by the accumulation of intracellular α-synuclein aggregates forming Lewy bodies and Lewy neurites. Consequently, PD is recognized as the most common synucleinopathy. The motor symptoms of the disease result from the progressive loss of dopaminergic neurons in the midbrain, leading to a significant dopamine deficit. Although PD has been studied extensively using traditional in vitro and in vivo...

item.title: Behavioral Analyses of Parkinson's Disease Model Mice
item.description: Parkinson's disease (PD) mice models have been generated to investigate the pathology of PD. Until now, we have reported dopaminergic (DA) neuron-specific autophagy-deficient mice and familial PD-associated gene mutant mice as models of PD. These mice provided in vivo evidence for PD pathology and motor dysfunction. In DA neuron-specific autophagy-deficient mice, this resulted in the formation of Lewy body. Consequently, DA neuron loss and motor dysfunction are observed in 120-week-old mice....

item.title: Monitoring PINK1-Parkin Signaling Using Dopaminergic Neurons from iPS Cells
item.description: The physiological importance of mitochondrial quality control has been uncovered by the finding that genes for early-onset Parkinson's disease (PD), PINK1 and Parkin, regulate mitochondrial autophagy, called mitophagy, and motility. Dopaminergic neurons derived from human induced pluripotent stem (iPS) cells are a useful tool for analyzing the pathogenesis caused by defects in mitochondrial quality control and for screening candidate drugs for PD. Moreover, dopaminergic neurons could provide new...

item.title: Neuron-Glia Co-Culture System for Parkinson's Disease Research
item.description: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disease characterized by motor symptoms, such as tremor, bradykinesia, rigidity, and postural instability due to a loss of nigrostriatal dopaminergic neurons. Glial cells, namely astrocytes and microglia, have received attention as key players in non-cell-autonomous pathological mechanisms in neurodegenerative diseases. On the other hand, glial cells protect neurons by releasing neurotrophic factors, producing antioxidants, and...

item.title: Preparation of Rat Primary Cortical Astrocyte Culture
item.description: Astrocytes and neurons originate from common neural stem cells, with astrocytes playing essential roles in neuronal survival. By forming the blood-brain barrier, astrocytes create a specialized metabolic environment that supports neuronal function. Traditionally, astrocytes have been classified as neurotoxic or neuroprotective subtypes based on gene expression and phenotypes, but their diversity across brain regions and functions renders this binary categorization insufficient. Increasing...

item.title: Detection of Substrate Phosphorylation of Leucine-Rich Repeat Kinase 2 in Tissues and Cultured Cells
item.description: Recent studies revealed that leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2) phosphorylates several Rab proteins under physiological conditions. Mutations linked with familial Parkinso'n disease cause an abnormal increase in the Rab phosphorylation, which has not been elucidated in an in vitro kinase assay where artificial peptide substrates are often used. Here, we provide protocols for detecting the LRRK2 activity in tissues and cultured cells using Rab phosphorylation as a readout.

item.title: Analysis of α-Synuclein in Cell-Type-Specific Extracellular Vesicles
item.description: α-Synuclein (α-Syn) is a key pathological protein in Parkinson's disease (PD) and related synucleinopathies. Recent evidence suggests that extracellular vesicles (EVs), particularly exosomes, contribute to the intercellular transmission of α-Syn and may serve as potential biomarkers. However, conventional EV isolation methods lack cell-type specificity, limiting their biological interpretability. In this chapter, we describe an optimized protocol for the isolation of cell-type-specific EVs...

item.title: Observation of α-Synuclein Droplets and Analysis of Aggregates Formed by Liquid-Liquid Phase Separation In Vitro
item.description: Aggregation of α-synuclein (αSyn) is a key event in the development of α-synucleinopathies, including Parkinson's disease and dementia with Lewy bodies. Recent studies have shown that αSyn undergoes liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) and subsequently forms aggregates through a sol-gel phase transition. In this chapter, we describe methods for observing αSyn LLPS and analyzing the resulting aggregates in vitro.

item.title: α-Synuclein Seeding Assay Using RT-QuIC
item.description: α-Synucleinopathies, including Parkinson's disease, dementia with Lewy bodies, and multiple system atrophy, are neurodegenerative disorders characterized by the misfolding and aggregation of α-synuclein (α-Syn). These conditions are thought to involve distinct conformational strains of αSyn aggregates that drive self-propagation and cell-to-cell transmission, with aggregation occurring via a seeded polymerization mechanism. The real-time quaking-induced conversion (RT-QuIC) assay, originally...

item.title: Safety and Effectiveness of Lisdexamfetamine Dimesylate in Paediatric Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Assessed by Physicians and School Teachers: A Post-marketing Surveillance Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Findings from this post-marketing surveillance study of LDX in paediatric patients with ADHD in Japan were consistent with its established safety profile. Patients' ADHD symptoms improved according to both physician and teacher assessments.

item.title: Crossing the biological hierarchy with 2D materials-based biomedical devices
item.description: Two-dimensional (2D) materials have attracted significant attention owing to their distinctive physicochemical properties arising from their ultrathin planar architectures. While the term "2D materials" is traditionally associated with atomically thin or few-layer systems, such as graphene, MXenes, and transition metal dichalcogenides, recent advances have demonstrated that materials with thicknesses spanning from several nanometers to micrometers can also exhibit characteristic two-dimensional...

item.title: Protocol of the randomized controlled trial of electronic Patient-Reported Outcome Monitoring with Integrated hospital-community pharmaciSt Engagement for diverse outpatient anticancer chemotherapy: the PRO-MISE trial
item.description: BACKGROUND: Patients receiving outpatient systemic anticancer therapy may develop symptoms between visits. Clinicians may under-recognize these symptoms, delaying supportive care and compromising health-related quality of life (HRQoL). We will test whether weekly smartphone-based electronic Patient-Reported Outcome (ePRO) monitoring linked to community-pharmacist review and structured communication with treating institutions improves HRQoL across diverse cancers.

item.title: Adverse Effects of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) Inhibitors in Pediatric Heart Failure: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Proportions
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: SGLT2 inhibitors had a tolerable safety profile in pediatric heart failure, mirroring the adult experience. Adequately powered randomized trials with standardized adverse-event grading are needed.

item.description: CONCLUSION: These findings support the involvement of Hedgehog and phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K) signaling in the pathogenesis of metastatic maxillary ameloblastoma and demonstrate the potential value of genetic profiling for identifying therapeutic targets in aggressive or metastatic odontogenic tumors.

item.title: Integrating morphology and spatial omics in gastric cancer: bridging classical mucin phenotypes and molecular stemness
item.description: Gastric cancer has been described through successive frameworks, each capturing a different dimension of the same heterogeneous tumor. The Lauren, World Health Organization, and Japanese Gastric Cancer Association report histological morphology; mucin phenotyping reports gastric versus intestinal lineage differentiation; and the The Cancer Genome Atlas and Asian Cancer Research Group classifications report molecular state. item.title: Structural and Conceptual Constraints Limiting Biological Invasion Management to Incremental Wins
item.description: The management of biological invasions is increasingly characterised by a sequence of incremental wins and recurring management losses, whereas invasion pressure, ecological impacts, and socio-economic costs continue to rise globally. Here, we propose that this pattern reflects systemic constraints in post-introduction management, rather than a lack of effort, knowledge, or intent. item.title: Tumor-expressed HNF1A promotes antitumor immunity by activating tumor-infiltrating CD8<sup>+</sup> T cells
item.description: The development of immune checkpoint inhibitors has improved the treatment outcomes for patients with many types of cancer. However, the clinical benefits remain limited in many patients, highlighting the need for novel therapeutic strategies to enhance antitumor immunity. Hepatocyte nuclear factor 1A (HNF1A) is a transcription factor that regulates the expression of several liver-specific genes, and its expression is increased in certain cancers, such as colon and non-small cell lung cancer...

item.title: CXCL12<sup>+</sup> LSEC-CXCR4<sup>+</sup> CAF axis drives post-transplant hepatocellular carcinoma recurrence under tacrolimus immunosuppression
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The CXCL12 + LSEC-CXCR4 + CAF interaction is vital in promoting post-transplant HCC recurrence. Blocking this axis could be a promising strategy for treating and preventing recurrence while preserving graft-protective immunosuppression.

item.title: Ultrasonographic findings at the end of failed hydrostatic reduction in pediatric intussusception: focus on the frond sign and immobility
item.description: CONCLUSION: Final ultrasonographic findings at the end of failed hydrostatic reduction may help characterize the residual intussusceptum. The frond sign was common, whereas persistent immobility was associated with bowel resection and was observed in both ileocolocolic cases.

item.title: Stage-tailored role of extrahepatic bile duct resection in gallbladder cancer: limited value in T2 disease and potential oncologic role in selected T3/T4 cases
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Routine EBDR appears unnecessary for T2 GBC. In T3/T4 disease, EBDR was associated with better OS and a lower observed frequency of local recurrence; however, these exploratory findings require validation in larger cohorts.

item.title: A Mitochondria-Targeted Fluorescent Probe for the Real-Time Tracking of Hypochlorous Acid During Inflammation
item.description: Hypochlorous acid (HOCl) is a key reactive oxygen species involved in redox and immune regulation. We report Mito-HOCl, a rationally designed naphthalimide-based probe for rapid, mitochondria-targeted HOCl detection. HOCl-induced oxidation of the thiomorpholine receptor suppresses photoinduced electron transfer (PET), causing a 20-fold fluorescence enhancement. item.title: Synthesis of C3-symmetric BN-embedded nanographene with 60 π-electrons and 32% BN content through a regioselective hexa-annulation reaction
item.description: We synthesized a C(3)-symmetric nanographene comprising a triphenylene core fused with three pyrene units through BN sequences via a one-pot, regioselective hexa-annulation. The resulting nanographene features a 60π-electron system and the highest BN content (31.6%) among well-defined graphenoids, with a weakly delocalized 54π global circuit spanning the BN-sequence boundaries.

item.title: Shorter Disease Duration Predicts Earlier Complete Skin Clearance in Biologic-naïve Psoriasis Treated with Biologics
item.description: The association between psoriasis disease duration and complete skin clearance after biologic initiation remains uncertain. item.description: Operating sulfide-based all-solid-state batteries (SSBs) at high voltages increases energy density but induces O2 release from cathode materials, degrading battery performance. item.title: Pathways to becoming a medical mycology specialist: A global Young ISHAM - EFISG survey of training, recognition, and workforce priorities
item.description: Fungal diseases are an increasing threat, yet training pathways in medical mycology (MM) remain poorly encouraged, defined and heterogeneous. We conducted a global survey to characterise specialist training, competencies, infrastructure, barriers, and priorities for MM education. We performed an international, cross-sectional, web-based survey, open from February to May 2026. item.title: High-resolution transcriptome analysis reveals a multilayered and dynamic transcriptional architecture in the archaeal virus SSV1
item.description: Members of Fuselloviridae infecting thermoacidophilic Sulfolobales are among the best-studied archaeal viruses, with the Saccharolobus spindle-shaped virus 1 (SSV1)-Saccharolobus solfataricus interaction serving as a model system. After infection, SSV1 establishes a chronic infection with new virions continuously budding from the infected cell. item.description: We analyze the conformational and dynamical properties of the kinetoplast DNA (kDNA), a massive sheet-like structure made from thousands of circular DNA molecules, found in the mitochondrion of certain parasites. The connectivity between circular DNA molecules is achieved by topological linking; hence, the kDNA may be regarded as a naturally occurring two-dimensional version of Olympic gels, whose physical properties are yet to be understood. item.title: Helical π-frameworks as tunable fluorescence-lifetime pressure chemical sensors
item.description: Helicene analogs enable fluorescence lifetime pressure sensing in solution. All five chemosensors showed linear lifetime increases under hydrostatic pressure, with sensitivity governed by molecular size, conformational freedom, and intermolecular quenching. Activation volume analysis revealed distinct pressure-response mechanisms, establishing helicenes as tunable molecular probes for quantitative mechanical sensing.

item.title: Additively Manufactured Implants for Mandibular Overdentures RCT Part 2: Functional and OHRQoL outcomes
item.description: This study evaluated and compared the functional outcomes and oral health-related quality of life (OHRQoL) associated with immediate and conventional loading protocols in a randomized clinical trial of mandibular overdentures supported by two additively manufactured narrow-diameter implants. item.description: Following development and evaluation of the Structured Problem Analysis of Raising Kids aged 36 months (SPARK36), this mixed-method study explored school nurses' perceived barriers and facilitators to its implementation in School Health Services in Flanders, Belgium. item.title: Comparative genomics reveals contrasting candidate adaptive signatures in two ecologically similar plateau fishes
item.description: Plateau aquatic environments expose fishes to chronic cold, hypoxia, ultraviolet radiation and low productivity, providing natural systems for studying genomic features associated with environmental adaptation. item.title: Audiovisual temporal asynchrony differentially influences material property and action quality judgements: Evidence for stable individual differences in material perception
item.description: In everyday life, audiovisual temporal correspondence, action quality and material properties are perceived simultaneously during natural interactions. item.description: Understanding children's numerosity perception is essential for identifying the cognitive foundations of early mathematical learning, yet traditional assessment methods remain lengthy and inefficient. item.description: CONCLUSION: KELIM provided prognostic information in Japanese HGSOC patients. Moreover, higher KELIM may identify greater chemosensitivity and absence of residual malignancy at IDS; prospective validation is required before clinical application.

item.description: CONCLUSION: Together, these results show significant variation in composition and host factors within the dysbiosis landscape, with potential implications for the interpretation of microbiome-based diagnostics and future microbiome-modulation studies.

item.description: Serpentinite-hosted ecosystems have been widely studied as analogues of early Earth environments, with particular emphasis on H(2)-fueled lithoautotrophy. item.title: Ventral tegmental area dopaminergic neurons contribute to hindlimb control during obstacle-avoidance locomotion in mice

item.description: Post-transplantation cyclophosphamide (PTCy)-based prophylaxis has become one of the most widely used strategies to prevent graft-versus-host disease (GVHD), particularly after HLA-haploidentical hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT). item.title: Overview of Plant Superoxide Dismutase Research: History to Horizon
item.description: Superoxide dismutases (SODs) are key components of the plant antioxidant network, acting alongside catalases, ascorbate peroxidases, peroxiredoxins, and other enzymes to control reactive oxygen species (ROS). Since their discovery in 1969, SODs have been defined by their ability to catalyze the dismutation of superoxide radicals into hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) and molecular oxygen. item.title: Autonomy without abandonment: the case for informed decisions in organized prostate cancer early detection
item.description: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: In most Western countries, prostate cancer early detection is not organized but left to "shared decision-making" between individual men and their physicians. We assess whether this approach can bear the ethical weight assigned to it and consider what respect for persons requires instead.
